name: Tureis
description: A star 19 parsecs away, 3.3 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 39757: radius 3.334 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 21.339 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.233) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 39757: effective temperature 6799 +/- 895 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.075)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 39757: distance 19.482 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.003), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 19 parsecs away, 3.3 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 21 times the Sun's luminosity at 6,799 K, so 3.334 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 39757: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Rho Puppis
quotes.card: Rho Puppis, formally named Tureis, is a star in the southern constellation of Puppis.
quotes.introduction: With an apparent visual magnitude of 2.7 or 2.8, it is the third-brightest member of this generally faint constellation.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 5698015743046182272 (quality A), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
